title: Compliance Bulletin: A Medicare Supplement Policy Pays Only Alongside Original Medicare
content:
A policy under Medicare Supplement Insurance Policies pays only alongside Original Medicare, so it is unlawful to sell one to a member who is enrolled in a Medicare Advantage plan unless they are leaving it.

### The condition on issue

No Medicare Advantage enrollment is in force for this member on the day the supplement policy would take effect. The member's enrollments in Medicare Advantage Health Plans — the enrollment itself, the member it belongs to and the status it stands at — are what settle this, correlated to the applicant by the member, and settled before the supplement policy is issued. An enrollment satisfies the condition where it stands as disenrolled, as terminated for non-payment, or as cancelled before it took effect.

### Where the member is leaving a Medicare Advantage plan

Where the member holds a Medicare Advantage plan the application is taken only where their disenrollment is already recorded and the supplement is dated to begin the day the Medicare Advantage coverage ends, so that there is no day on which both are in force.

### Where the member is keeping it

A member who keeps their Medicare Advantage plan is told plainly that a supplement would pay them nothing, and the application is not taken however firmly they ask.

### Drug coverage held alongside

Holding a stand-alone Part D drug plan alongside a supplement is perfectly proper, because no supplement sold today carries drug coverage; the two are billed and serviced entirely apart.

### The trial right

A member inside their first year of a first Medicare Advantage plan has a trial right to return to Original Medicare with a guaranteed issue right to a supplement, and the plan checks their enrolment history rather than taking their word for the trial right.
